Method of Attack: Encrypts files using AES (CRT mode) with a unique 64-character ASCII key per execution
Terminates specific services and processes including Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS), data backup services, and anti-malware products to facilitate encryption
Clears console and Windows system logs to prevent forensic analysis
Excludes system-critical files and folders to keep the system operational for ransom note display
Double-extortion tactic by stealing data and threatening to publish if ransom is not paid
Impacted Systems: Windows systems (implied by Windows system logs and services mentioned)
Organizations worldwide including victims in USA, France, Israel, Turkey, Czech Republic, Algeria, Egypt, and Peru
Attack Vector: Unknown exact infection point; possible exploit, phishing emails, or other means
Indicators of Compromise: Ransom note is an 8-page PDF last modified on February 9, 2023
Ransom demand of $10,000 in XMR (Monero) cryptocurrency
Use of qTox messenger for attacker communication
Dark web data leak site listing victims
Tor site for ransom portal (currently offline)
